test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 20 March, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'** i.e. **'Them'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **most appropriate option **to fill in the blank No. 2 is **"them".**
 
• **In the context **of the sentence,** "them" **refers to the guard's wrists that have been yanked up behind his back.
 
• The** plural pronoun** "them" **agrees **with the plural noun **"wrists."**
 
• Therefore, the part of the sentence with the blank would read, "and locked them together with a pair of handcuffs."

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'The man with the shotgun pushed the guard to his knees. He handed up the shotgun to his partner and yanked the guard's wrists up behind his back and locked **them **together with a pair of handcuffs. He (3) ______ him onto the floor with a kick between the shoulder blades. Then he took his shotgun back and (4) ______ to the security gate at the end of the counter. He was short and heavy and moved with peculiar slowness. “Buzz him (5) ______,” his partner said.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's see why the other options are less suitable:
 
 
• **"That" **is a singular demonstrative pronoun, so it doesn't match the plural noun "wrists."
 
• **"These" **is a plural demonstrative pronoun, but it is typically used when the speaker is referring to something near them, not suitable here.
 
• **"It"** is a singular pronoun, which again does not agree in number with the plural "wrists."
